AUV has two common meanings depending on context. In automotive contexts, especially in the Philippines and parts of Asia, AUV stands for Asian Utility Vehicle, a multi-passenger body style designed primarily for carrying people and sometimes goods, historically overlapping with MPVs and sometimes used interchangeably with them [d1,d2,d5]. In marine and oceanographic contexts, AUV stands for Autonomous Underwater Vehicle, which is an unmanned, untethered robot that operates independently underwater using preprogrammed instructions and onboard sensors [d3,d4,d6,d7,d8]. Because these meanings belong to different domains and are not in conflict, the term is best interpreted by clarifying whether the discussion is about cars or underwater vehicles.
